guards: Suppression has to mean removal from what SHIPPED, not an entry in a list. SuppressedClaims is what the Verification Pass/Fail panel counts, so a verifier that recorded the claim and delivered it anyway would leave every live instrument reading healthy while an uncited creatinine reached the cardiologist - the confidently-stated hallucination REQUIREMENTS.md 3.2 calls a patient-safety event rather than a UX blemish. It also pins that suppression is per line: the two cited lines beside the bad one still ship.

answer.intent: A draft that asserts a specific clinical value with no citation: FR-VERIF-1 must remove that line from what ships, while the cited lines beside it survive.
